newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P assigns A+ rating to Petronas samurai bonds.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns A+ rating to Petronas samurai bonds.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp (S&P) said on Monday that it had assigned an A+ long-term foreign currency rating to Petroliam Nasional Berhad's (Petronas) 22 billion yen samurai bond issue.
Petronas's bond issue was in two tranches. The first was an eight billion yen five-year bond priced at 2.70 percent, and the other was a 14 billion yen 10-year issue priced at 3.60 percent.
The Malaysian national oil company's offer precedes a $1.9 billion three-tranche issue, rated A+, in the Yankee bond market in October 1996.

The Yankee bond issue was $600 million worth of five-year bonds, priced at 6.625 percent, $800 million worth of 10-year bonds, priced at 7.125 percent, and $500 million worth of 30-year bonds priced at 7.625 percent.
The proceeds from these offerings will be used to refinance existing foreign-currency borrowings and finance a portion of the capital expenditure for new projects.
At the same time, S&P said it had affirmed the A+ foreign currency and AA+ local currency ratings on Petronas.
It also said the outlook was positive.
